title: Separate the variables
text: Move everything with $$y$$ to one side with dy, and everything with the other variable to the other side, then integrate both sides.

title: Integrate and solve
text: The integral of $$\frac{1}{y^2+4}$$ is $$\frac{1}{2} \arctan\left(\frac{y}{2}\right)$$, so $$\frac{1}{2} \arctan\left(\frac{y}{2}\right)=x^3+C$$. At $$x=0$$, $$y=0$$ this gives $$C=0$$. So $$\arctan\left(\frac{y}{2}\right)=2x^3$$ and $$y=2tan\left(2x^3\right)$$.
